name: chown
description: Changes the owner and/or group of files and directories. Requires root for changing owners.

flags.description: Change only files currently owned by OLD.

examples.explanation: Gives file.txt to user, keeping the current group.
Hands a web root to the web server user and group — the classic nginx/apache setup step.
Recursively fixes ownership of an entire project tree, e.g. after extracting an archive as root.
Changes only the group, keeping the owner.

about: Only root can give a file away or take it; regular users may change the group to one they belong to. Ownership matters because permissions are evaluated per triad: if the web server cannot read your files, the first thing to check is the owner.
useCases: Assign files to service accounts (www-data, postgres).
Fix ownership after copying files as root or extracting archives.
mistakes: Forgetting sudo — chown to another user fails without root.
Recursive chown on system directories like / or /usr, which breaks the system.
warnings: Never run chown -R on / or system paths. Incorrect ownership of /usr, /etc, or /var can render the system unbootable.
